images.filename: COLLECTIE TROPENMUSEUM 'Het standbeeld van J.P. Coen voor het Paleis van Daendels het 'Grote Huis' aan het Waterlooplein in Weltevreden te Batavia' TMnr 10015443.jpg
images.caption: Negatif. Gedung yang terletak di salah satu sisi Waterlooplein (Lapangan Waterloo, sekarang Lapangan Banteng) ini seharusnya adalah Istana Daendels namun tidak pernah selesai. Meskipun demikian, hal ini adalah inisiatif yang penting, karena orang-orang Eropa yang menghuni pusat kota Batavia (Kota Lama) mulai tidak sehat (serangan malaria) dan cenderung pergi dari sana. Sekitar tahun 1900, Weltevreden (sekarang Gambir) mulai dibangun dan selesai sekitar tahun 1920, demikian pula  kawasan Menteng, yang terletak lebih jauh ke selatan. Saat ini, orang-orang kaya Indonesia tinggal di sana. Di gedung ini kantor pemerintah Daendels berada dan sekarang masih berdiri (menjadi gedung Departemen Keuangan, namun patung Coen di sebelah kiri sudah disingkirkan sejak masa pendudukan Jepang). [Kutipan, dengan sedikit tambahan, dari P. Boomgaard 1921]

images.filename: Diest-Gate.jpg
images.caption:
View of the Diestpoort see from the south. 
To the right slaves bathe horses in the river. A bastion on a small island in the river in front of the gate was built to protect against a possible threat from the nearby Chinese quarter. The Chinese population was rounded up and concentrated here in 1740 in the aftermath of the Chinese uprising and the massacre that followed. The area between the walls and the Chinese quarter was purposely left unoccupied. 
To the right of centre two imams take a stroll, accompanied by a slave boy bearing a parasol. 
Cf. National Library of Indonesia, inv.nr. A 08.
The roof of the inner hospital can be seen to the right of the picture. The tower of the New Church is visible at center.

images.filename: Pasar-Bamboo-along-Buitengracht.jpg
images.caption:
View of the Pasar Bambu, seen from the south. 

A sluice in the Buitengracht, or outer canal, has been built to regulate the water levels in the southern city canal. The lock comprises four smaller sluices, known as 'boerenverdrieten' (farmers' sorrows). 

To the left of the sluice is the bamboo market. Bamboo was used as a cheap building material. Depicted in the foreground is a man bearing a long bamboo pole.

Far left is the Utrecht Gate. Far right is the Nassau bastion and further the Diest Gate and the roof of the inner hospital.
